reason: The protocol holds up; it is the right fix for PC13-03. It is logically sound, costs no slot and no GPU, and has no knob, so R8 and byte-identity do not apply. Checks: (a) Public bests never go down, and merged or deleted teams disappear rather than rank below us. So 'a team from A0 now ranks below us' proves that our unrounded best rose, whatever other teams do. PC13-03's extra 'same Score and SubmissionCount' condition only cost power. The test is one-sided and weak: B0 is the team best, which is P36 (P36 unrounded > #35; K2 passed nobody, 6th/73 -> 12th/87), and P36 already contains lp30. Still, UP => probe > B0 >= K2, so every UP is real and NEU is the safe default, which is good for private. (c) The latency arithmetic is correct: 39 at 04:37-04:48Z, 40 at 04:39-04:50Z, 41 at 05:00-05:11Z, 42 at 07:27-07:38Z. (d) and (e) are right: no common-knob credit, and after an UP the next probe has to beat the new best. Value is small but real. It is the input that L5v2 (R13L-1) and the A-only 0.954 extension (R13L-3) need, and without it every 0.954 display is NEU by default. Weak points that need fixing, not refuting: (1) Freshness keyed on LastSubmissionDate has unverified semantics and depends on the order of completion. Our LB SubmissionCount stayed at 40 at 16:20, 20:01 and 22:46Z although 39-41 were submitted 21:15-21:38Z, so it counts SCORED submissions only. That makes it a better key that does not depend on order and also detects co-completion. (2) The fixed windows can miss events. Dummy runtimes relative to K2 run from 0.87x (exp70d) to 1.15x (exp70b), so exp70b could arrive around 08:30Z, after 07:50Z. (3) The 2-min window for 42 is unnecessary. 42 scores alone, so there is no co-completion risk, and the rule does not care what other teams do. The window also overlaps the morning-push timer (~07:30Z). (4) The extra ListSubmissions calls add risk of HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests), as seen at 20:36:50Z. A 429 line in poll.log blocks submits under W6. The watcher has to stay clear of lb_poll's call and give way to an E10 trigger (R12-A4 (5)).
fix: Log (a)-(f) with L5v2 before 04:37Z, with these amendments. (1) S0: any LB download taken after our last score change and before the event works, so the 22:46Z or 03:04Z E10 snapshot can be S0 for event 1. A fresh 04:10Z download is optional. For later events, the previous S1 is the next S0. (2) FRESHNESS: S1 is valid iff our row's SubmissionCount == 40 + (number of ladder probes COMPLETE in ListSubmissions at download time). LastSubmissionDate is a secondary check. If stale, re-download every 2 min up to 3 times, then AMBIGUOUS (= NEU). At the first event, record whether an ERROR increments the count. (3) WINDOWS are event-driven. Poll ListSubmissions every 120 s from 04:10Z while at least 2 of 56589025/56589065/56589423 are PENDING, then every 300 s until all three are terminal (hard cap 06:45Z). No 2-min watcher for 42: take one LB download right after the first poll.log header that shows 56592350 COMPLETE (cap 09:40Z, i.e. 9.5 h + 5 min). Skip any watcher call within 60 s of lb_poll's hh:x9 call. (4) API precedence: an E10 trigger pauses the watcher (R12-A4 (5)). On a 429, back off 60 s at most twice, then pause 10 min, and never let the watcher run within 15 min before a submit (W6). The round-14/15 browser agents must not run e10_snapshot during the active watch. (5) An ERROR status change needs no S1, and a COMPLETE that co-occurs with an ERROR is attributable. (6) Record per event: S0/S1 file names, SubmissionCount, refs that changed status, passed TeamIds (info), verdict UP/NEU/AMBIGUOUS. lb_poll.py is untouched and poll.log stays the L9 record.
realistic_gain: No direct score gain. It is a measurement protocol. It prevents a wrong or untestable in-block read that would otherwise decide L5v2's combo rung (P(submitted) ~0.03-0.06) and R13L-3's exp70a finals swap (expected private ~+0.00005..+0.0001, a few ranks at most). Cost: ~30-60 read-only API calls plus 3-5 LB downloads and ~1 h of main-session work. There is a small 429 risk, which the precedence rules contain.
